title: Booking API integration tests on Testcontainers
name: Booking integration tests

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these integration tests isolate their data from one another? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why can't the test class simply be annotated with @Transactional to roll back each test's changes, given that requests go through TestRestTemplate on a RANDOM_PORT server?
choices: The embedded server handles each request on its own thread with its own transaction, so the test's rollback cannot undo what the server commits
Because TestRestTemplate disables transactions in the application
Because @Transactional only works with H2 and not with PostgreSQL
Because Testcontainers wraps every statement in an autocommit transaction

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of @DynamicPropertySource combined with the container started in the static initializer?
choices: It restarts the container for every test method to guarantee a clean database
It supplies the JDBC URL, user and password of the container's randomly mapped port to the Spring context at startup, and the single container is shared by all subclasses in the JVM
It replaces the Flyway migrations with a schema generated from the entities
It makes Spring connect to a Postgres instance already running on localhost:5432

questions.prompt: What does createBooking_forTakenSeat_returnsConflict actually verify about the application?
choices: That two concurrent requests for the same seat result in exactly one booking
That a second sequential request for an already held seat is rejected with 409, using the real Postgres schema and constraints
That the first request returns 201, and that bookings are idempotent
That the service retries when the database is unavailable
